finding: Authoring is complete against the blueprint on a nominal count, but Areas 1, 2 and 4 carry ZERO slack. Every pending question in Areas 2 and 4 must survive its first independent audit for Batch 3 to reach 360 in one pass.

observed_first_audit_pass_rate.note: Every failure so far was recovered by a narrow repair and a focused reaudit under a new auditor instance, so failures cost audit CYCLES rather than capacity. With zero slack, though, a single failure blocks the area until its repair round completes.

consequence: At the observed rate the Area-2 pool of 67 pending questions expects about three first-audit failures and the Area-4 pool of 14 expects about one, and neither area can absorb any. Batch 3 would therefore need at least one repair-and-reaudit round in each of Areas 2 and 4 before reaching 360. That is survivable but serialised, and every round depends on an auditor being dispatched.

controller_recommendation.why_this_is_not_padding: The instruction was to author only the minimum necessary and not to create questions merely because identifiers were reserved. A buffer sized to the project's own measured attrition rate is part of the minimum: authoring exactly 360 when about 5% of first audits fail makes a one-pass 360 arithmetically unlikely rather than merely uncertain.
